Conceptual spillover model is background, not validated forecast; CDC multi-month guidance background for one-dose cure; NIH secondary LongCOVID summary background after linked primary body unreadable. RIO delayed rebound is not reservoir eradication; teixobactin no-mutant observation not resistance impossibility; R21 multidose finite efficacy not sterilizing/lifelong; gene-drive cages/models not field vector elimination; PhagoBurn negative outcome not universal therapeutic success. Replaced ellipsis pseudoquote with actual contiguous sentence.

sourceChecks.title: Identification of Broad-Spectrum Antiviral Compounds by Targeting Viral Entry
sourceChecks.paraphrase: A compound-screening study found inhibitors active against several virus families and tested selected candidates in a Zika mouse model; authors describe the work as proof of concept.
sourceChecks.limitations: Tests cover selected viruses and cell/animal models, not all RNA and DNA viruses. Some compounds showed toxicity; the paper says in-vivo safety/dosing needs empirical evaluation and anticipates cocktails.

sourceChecks.title: Time to HIV rebound after infusion of long-acting broadly neutralising antibodies 3BNC117-LS and 10-1074-LS and analytical treatment interruption (the RIO trial)
sourceChecks.excerpt: 75% of participants in arm A did not have viral rebound
sourceChecks.paraphrase: A randomized phase 2 trial found longer ART-free viral control after two broadly neutralizing antibodies for some early-treated adults; most treated participants had not rebounded at week 20.
sourceChecks.limitations: This delayed rebound but did not eradicate HIV reservoirs or establish functional cure; cohort was 68 early-treated adults selected for viral sensitivity, with 20-week follow-up.

sourceChecks.title: Prediction of viral spillover risk based on the mass action principle
sourceChecks.excerpt: this is primarily a conceptual exercise
sourceChecks.paraphrase: A conceptual spatial risk model combines zoonotic-virus diversity and human-population density to identify regions potentially at higher spillover risk.
sourceChecks.limitations: It does not forecast a particular genome’s spillover probability, evolutionary trajectory, or future transmissibility in real time; model validation and field forecasting are not demonstrated.

sourceChecks.title: A new antibiotic kills pathogens without detectable resistance
sourceChecks.excerpt: We did not obtain any mutants of Staphylococcus aureus or Mycobacterium tuberculosis resistant to teixobactin.
sourceChecks.paraphrase: Teixobactin binds conserved cell-wall precursors; the study could not obtain resistant S. aureus or M. tuberculosis mutants in its tested experiments.
sourceChecks.limitations: A result under specified laboratory conditions does not show resistance is impossible, cover all bacteria or bypass pathways, or establish a clinically deployed class that ends AMR.

sourceChecks.title: Clinical Overview of Latent Tuberculosis Infection
sourceChecks.excerpt: Three months of once-weekly isoniazid plus rifapentine (3HP)
sourceChecks.paraphrase: CDC lists effective latent-TB regimens that last three or four months, as well as six to nine month alternatives.
sourceChecks.limitations: These are multi-dose preventive regimens with risk reduction, not a one-dose cure of active and latent TB or >95% eradication.

sourceChecks.title: Safety and efficacy of malaria vaccine candidate R21/Matrix-M in African children: a multicentre, double-blind, randomised, phase 3 trial
sourceChecks.excerpt: Vaccines were administered as three doses, 4 weeks apart, with a booster administered 12 months after the third dose.
sourceChecks.paraphrase: Phase 3 trial of 4,878 vaccinated children in four African countries used three primary doses and a booster at 12 months; 12-month clinical malaria efficacy was 75% at seasonal and 68% at standard sites, with modest waning.
sourceChecks.limitations: Efficacy was against clinical malaria in children in trial regions, not sterile immunity, all Plasmodium stages, lifelong protection, single dose, all age groups or global eradication.

sourceChecks.title: Dual effector population modification gene-drive strains of the African malaria mosquitoes, Anopheles gambiae and Anopheles coluzzii
sourceChecks.excerpt: support the further development of TP13-based strains
sourceChecks.paraphrase: Researchers tested CRISPR gene-drive mosquito lines and parasite-blocking effectors in laboratory strains/cages and modeled a conceptual island release; resistance alleles and fitness effects were observed/considered.
sourceChecks.limitations: Laboratory cages and modeled release are not safe, scalable field elimination. The paper describes fitness loads, drive-resistant alleles, model assumptions, strain-specific results, and work remaining before field release.

sourceChecks.title: Immune system may attack nervous system in some Long COVID patients
sourceChecks.locator: At a Glance and study findings, lines 17–28
sourceChecks.excerpt: More research is needed to link specific autoantibodies to particular Long COVID symptoms.
sourceChecks.paraphrase: NIH summarizes a Cell study connecting specific autoantibodies with some neurologic symptoms, with antibody-transfer experiments in mice; the source says more research is needed.
sourceChecks.limitations: One proposed pathway in a subset does not establish a unifying mechanism for all postviral syndromes or a safe prophylactic intervention.

sourceChecks.title: Efficacy and tolerability of a cocktail of bacteriophages to treat burn wounds infected by Pseudomonas aeruginosa (PhagoBurn)
sourceChecks.excerpt: The trial was stopped ... because of the insufficient efficacy of PP1131.
sourceChecks.paraphrase: A randomized phase 1/2 trial compared topical phage cocktail with standard care in Pseudomonas burn wounds; it stopped for insufficient efficacy after phage titer fell below the intended dose.
sourceChecks.limitations: One pathogen-specific cocktail, indication, and route do not show a programmable off-the-shelf platform for every bacterium, 100% specificity, or reliable clinical outcomes.
